title: Savio to showcase smart spinning and winding at India ITME 2026
content:
Savio will showcase Proxima Smartconer, Lybra Smartspinner, Phoenix Assembly Winder and SIRIUS TFO twisting solutions at INDIA ITME 2026 for Indian mills.
The technologies target higher efficiency, flexibility, yarn quality, low energy use and remote monitoring through Savio Insight.
Lybra supports multi-blend air-jet spinning, while Phoenix and Sirius aid package formation and TFO twisting.

title: India’s cotton yarn stable on slow demand despite firm prices
content:
South India cotton yarn prices stayed stable in Mumbai and Tiruppur as sluggish fabric demand and tight payment flows curbed buying.
Spinning mills sought support from firmer cotton, but slow downstream demand prevented yarn price increases.
Gujarat cotton rose ₹1,000-1,200 per candy, guided by higher ICE cotton, with all-India arrivals at 130,000-135,000 bales.

title: Mario Crosta to highlight textile finishing technology at India ITME
content:
Italian textile machinery manufacturer Mario Crosta will participate in India ITME 2026 at Hall 16, Booth A7, highlighting fabric surface finishing technologies.
Founded in 1925, the company has installed over 10,000 machines across 75 countries.
Its solutions serve knitted, woven, wool and home textiles, with an emphasis on innovation, energy efficiency and sustainable processing.

title: Ferraro to highlight fabric finishing solutions at India ITME 2026
content:
Italy’s Ferraro SpA will participate in India ITME 2026 at Hall 16, Booth A4, highlighting machinery for tubular and open-width fabric finishing.
Established in 1951, the company offers HOT FIXING, EASY COMPTEX, COMPTEX REvolution, X-SLIT and other specialised solutions, focusing on fabric dimensional stability, consistent finishing quality and processing efficiency.

title: €58 mn denim shift raises stakes for Egypt, China and Bangladesh
content:
Bangladesh remains the European Union's top denim supplier, but imports from the country fell 5.48 per cent to $1.10 billion in January to September 2026.
Egypt gained $63.6 million, almost matching Bangladesh's $63.4 million loss, while China rose 20.23 per cent and Turkey lost $137.7 million.
TexPro trouser data and Egypt's garment network point to a 2027 contest over finishing and speed.

title: UK's Coats targets 2026 EBIT margin near 20% as profits stay resilient
content:
UK's Coats expects full-year organic revenue to be broadly flat and earnings before interest and tax margin at or above 20 per cent, while strong free cash flow is set to reduce year-end leverage to around 2.0 times.
Revenue was flat organically in the four months to October 31, as apparel grew 3 per cent and footwear fell 7 per cent amid more pronounced destocking by brands.
